The clip — extracted from Mulcahy's long-form 'The Tubes Video' — aired during MTV's earliest weeks, generating measurable sales spikes in Midwestern cable markets before the channel reached New York or Los Angeles. The video's corporate-satire aesthetic directly embodied the album's conceptual theme: a parody of Reagan-era 'Morning in America' salesmanship, with the band dressed as slick businessmen. The song was itself composed using the 'Completion Backward Principle' — its title came before its music — mirroring the motivational speaker's sales philosophy the album was built around.

As one of the channel's earliest rotation staples and a documented driver of regional record sales, it serves as primary evidence for the medium's commercial power. Mulcahy's direction and the corporate-parody concept give it both aesthetic and sociological research value. The Grammy-nominated long-form source work adds further archival significance.
H-rEVVAw3-0.sig: A landmark artifact in New Wave and early MTV history, 'Talk To Ya Later' is one of the first songs whose commercial success can be directly attributed to music video rotation rather than radio airplay. Produced by David Foster with guitar by Steve Lukather, it bridged theater rock, power pop, and corporate new wave. Its Mulcahy-directed video helped establish the template for high-concept, studio-produced performance clips in the nascent MTV era.
